name: Memority
abstract: French identity and access management vendor offering the Memority Identity Factory, a SaaS platform unifying identity governance and administration (IGA), SSO and federation, multi-factor authentication, and customer identity (CIAM) for employees, partners, customers, IoT, and non-human identities such as service accounts and AI agents. The platform is split into MY-Identity (lifecycle and rights governance), MY-Access (SSO and federation via SAML 2.0, WS-Federation, OAuth 2.0, and OpenID Connect, with risk-based adaptive authentication), MY-Keys (second-factor management: TOTP, WebAuthn/FIDO2, push, X.509), and MY-Discovery (shadow SaaS and ghost account discovery). Extensible through Groovy rules and actions and OAuth2-protected REST APIs. Hosted in Europe (Paris or Dublin) on AWS, S3NS (SecNumCloud 3.2), or GCP; ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 certified, with NIS2 and DORA compliance support. Pricing is quote-based.

plans.name: Memority Identity Factory (MY-Identity, MY-Access, MY-Keys, MY-Discovery)

features.description: Login and password authentication, using either a password stored in Memority (Memority Password module) or one held in the customer's Active Directory or LDAP directory.
Customers can sign in with social networks (Meta, Google, X, FranceConnect, b.connect) or any OAuth2/OpenID Connect provider through delegation modules, with automatic profile data enrichment.

WebAuthn authentication, including Windows Hello and YubiKey, with a global setting restricting registration to platform, cross-platform, or all authenticators; passkeys are listed on the product pages.
An OTP-by-mail module (configurable length, lifetime, and send/validate quotas) can be used as an authentication mechanism; it is documented mainly as a fallback factor.
An OTP-by-SMS module (configurable length, lifetime, and send/validate quotas) can be used as an authentication mechanism; it is documented mainly as a fallback factor.
Not documented in Memority's public product, security, or technical documentation.
Not documented in Memority's public product, security, or technical documentation.
TOTP is supported through the OATH module and Google or Microsoft Authenticator, as well as Memority's own browser and mobile OTP generators in MY-Keys Premium.
Not documented in Memority's public product, security, or technical documentation.
FIDO2 and YubiKey are documented through the WebAuthn module; legacy U2F is not named explicitly.
WebAuthn (FIDO2) is an authentication module that can be chained as a second factor in a two-factor authentication mechanism.
OTP by mail module with configurable maximum registrations, OTP length (default 4), lifetime (default 1 minute), and send/validate quota policies.
OTP by SMS module with configurable maximum registrations, OTP length (default 4), lifetime (default 1 minute), and send/validate quota policies.
Not documented in Memority's public product, security, or technical documentation.
Mobile push authentication through the Memority MFA module in mobile mode with push enabled (MY-Keys Premium), alongside fingerprint biometrics on iOS and Android.

Risk-based authentication computes a 0 to 100 risk score from device, location, and behavior, and only offers authentication mechanisms strong enough to bring the score under the application's tolerance.
Third-party MFA products can be connected through APIs, and RADIUS server or client authentication is supported; Cisco Duo is not named specifically.
Authentication mechanisms carry an authentication level, and risk-based authentication enforces step-up with a one-time password or another strong factor when the risk exceeds the threshold.

Memority acts as an OAuth2/OpenID Connect provider with per-application federations, JWT access tokens, standard and custom scopes, claims, and ACR/AMR values; it can also delegate to external OIDC providers.
SAML 2.0 identity provider federations with configurable NameID, additional attributes, signed assertions, requests, and logout messages, and downloadable IdP metadata.
WS-Federation relying-party federations with realm, assertion consumer URLs, NameID, additional attributes, and signed assertions.
The OAuth2 client credentials grant is supported for non-human identities such as services, connectors, and scripts.
External OAuth2/OpenID Connect providers can be plugged in through a provider authentication module with account mapping, optional PKCE, and custom scopes; Memority can also act as an IdP proxy.

External SAML 2.0 identity providers can be plugged in through a SAML2 provider authentication module (NameID format, REDIRECT or POST binding, signing certificate), and partners can authenticate through their own IdP.
Active Directory and LDAP authentication modules (LDAPS, up to two servers for high availability) plus Kerberos transparent authentication, and AD/LDAP provisioning connectors.
Federation and provisioning for Office 365 and Azure domains (accounts and licenses); MY-Discovery also has a native Microsoft Entra ID connector.
A native CSV import engine does mass creation, modification, and deletion of identities from multiple authoritative sources, and a REST bulk API handles batch operations.
Not documented in Memority's public product, security, or technical documentation.
Reports can be exported to CSV or XLSX and audit data can be pulled through a REST API; a dedicated bulk identity export is not documented.
The REST bulk API supports PATCH and DELETE on objects targeted by id, id list, or search expression, in transactional batches of 5000 operations by default.
The bulk API has a CREATE_OR_UPDATE operation, and CSV reconciliation uses correlation rules to match source rows to existing identities.

Users edit their profile, change or reset their password, enroll devices and MFA, and answer security questions from the self-service portal.
Identities authenticated through an external OIDC or SAML provider are mapped to Memority identities through an account mapping attribute; manual linking by users is not documented.
Identities can be suspended (blocked) as an emergency measure, deactivated, soft deleted, and reactivated.
Attributes are fully configurable per object type (Identity, Organization, Resource, Role, Role Publication), with translations, help texts, and reference tables.

Search expressions drive bulk operations, conditions, and tenant-wide audit filters; the portal search model is not documented in detail.
Role-based access with role requests, approval workflows, role publication, and segregation-of-duties policies.
Organizations are managed objects with several independent organization trees and internal, external, and partner identity types; tenant isolation is at application level.
Password policies set length (2 to 128), character classes and per-class minimums, repeated characters, regular expressions, history and reuse delay, expiry with grace period, and dictionaries.
Logins may only contain a-z, A-Z, 0-9 and the characters . - _ + ~ @.
Progressive data collection during customer journeys, limited to what each step requires.
Contextual access policies based on attributes, roles, schedules, geolocation, device, and user behavior; federations can restrict access through per-application access rights.
Rights can carry dimensions that limit their management scope (for example by organization or country), and API access is granted per API zone through the sys.api-zone-access right.
API Guardian authorizes calls per API zone for callers presenting an OAuth2 access token, in addition to the rights required on the target service.
SOC 2 Type II is a stated compliance goal, not yet a held certification.
Memority is certified ISO 27001, along with ISO 27701 and AirCyber Gold.

Identities go through soft delete (archived for a configurable 6 to 12 months) and hard delete (irreversible wipe); GDPR-specific anonymization is not documented.
Granular management and revocation of customer consent for data sharing with third parties, through the self-service portal.
Hosting regions Paris and Dublin on a provider of choice among AWS, S3NS, and GCP; the S3NS cloud is SecNumCloud 3.2 qualified.
A shared or dedicated platform option is offered, hosted on a public trusted cloud rather than customer-managed infrastructure.

All servers use encryption at rest; secrets are held in HSM modules and passwords use a dedicated non-reversible attribute.
All internal and external flows are encrypted; LDAPS and HTTPS are mandatory for provisioning connectors.

Login customization options include a remember-me switch (cookie valid 365 days by default) and a change-account button, alongside portal themes, assets, and fragments.

Online identity verification (KYC) through partners such as Docaposte, IDnow, and Tessi, identity document upload, and e-signature of terms through Yousign and DocuSign.
